DA hike: Why is there delay in DA hike announcement and when can government make it?
 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 21, 2026, 05:55:58 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 DA hike announcement: Central government employees are eagerly anticipating an announcement regarding a dearness allowance hike, which remains uncertain. The recent weekly meeting, where such an announcement could have taken place, was not convened. In response, the Confederation of Central Government Employees and Workers staged a protest highlighting the overdue DA hike. While previous discussions centered around performance-linked bonuses, the DA hike was overlooked. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online The dearness allowance hike for July 2026 is yet to be announced. Central government employees have long been waiting for a dearness allowance (DA) hike for July 2026, but they may have to wait longer, as the government hasn’t announced it so far. The government didn’t hold its weekly meeting on Wednesday, where the possibility of the DA hike announcement was high.
However, the DA hike announcement doesn’t require a cabinet meeting and can be made by the Finance Ministry without it.
Ever since the Labour Bureau announced the All India Consumer Price Index (Industrial Workers) for June 2026 on July 31, central government employees have been waiting for the DA hike announcement. Their expectations have been high in October’s cabinet meetings. 
In its previous meeting on October 14, the government announced performance-linked bonus (PLB) for Railway employees and didn’t say anything about the DA hike.
Two days later, on October 16, the Centre declared the non-performance-linked bonus for central government employees, but didn’t touch upon the DA hike topic. The government didn’t make any announcement ahead of Dussehra, which fell on October 20.
Officials associated with some employee associations predicted that the government might decide it after the cabinet meeting on Wednesday. However, an official later told ET Wealth that no meeting took place today.
Now it is to be seen when the government announces it.

 Govt order date DA rate (%) DA hike (%)

 April 2, 2025 55% 2% 
 October 21, 2024 53% 3% 
 March 12, 2024 50% 4%

 Source: Finance Ministry 
The government announces the DA hike twice a year. The hike depends on the 12-month average inflation index . For the January hike, the 12-month index reading is taken from January to December of the previous year.
For the July DA hike, the index is counted from July of the previous year to June of the same year.
 Expected DA hike for July 2026 
The current DA rate for central government employees is 60%. They will receive the hike as per the 12-month average retail inflation data (July 2025-June 2026). As per the average retail inflation, the estimated DA hike for July 2026 can be 3%, which can take the DA rate to 63%.
 Government employees’ protest for delay in DA hike 
The Confederation of Central Government Employees and Workers, a prominent employees’ body, on October 16 also demonstrated a lunch-hour protest at workplaces to demand the DA hike announcement.
In its letter dated October 14 sent to the cabinet secretary, central government, the confederation said that the demonstration was to ask the government to immediately declare the due instalment of DA and dearness relief (DR) with effect from July 1, 2026, for employees and pensioners and the announcement of ad-hoc and PLB bonus for the financial year 2025-26.
While the government announced the PLB the next day, it has yet to announce the DA hike. (Join our ETWealth WhatsApp channel for all the latest updates)
